title: Define Product Card 02 visual architecture then website components
objective: Develop Product Card 02 as a two-phase programme: first lock one narrow portrait website-card architecture and the bounded visual treatments it may use; then derive the complete responsive website component family for discovery, feature, pricing, checkout, bundle, upsell and post-purchase contexts.

included: Phase A round 02: one 320–360px portrait website-card architecture
four contextual treatments: Editorial Portrait, Full Field Portrait, System Index and Product Pack
desktop shelf, feature and mobile placement proof
role-based light and charcoal surface allocation
family shelf versus bundle offer semantics
single Living Core allocation with exact fallback
explicit Phase B website component and flow map
excluded: Phase B implementation before Phase A approval
production Stripe fields or revenue code

acceptance: one portrait architecture and four treatments are machine-checkable
Phase B website components are explicit and held until visual lock
four visibly credible AI OS card treatments inside real website contexts
desktop shelf, focal feature and mobile proof
canonical light and charcoal surface matrix
family shelf and bundle offer examples
preference receipt for the Phase A gate

verification.passCondition: the portrait card is clearly the website component being reviewed and remains recognisable across four treatments
candidates are shown in website shelves, focal features, catalogues, commerce and mobile placements rather than as isolated art cards
calm same-polarity and focal cross-contrast allocations use canonical F8, #171715, #1B1B19 and #252523 surfaces
family shelf means comparing equal products and bundle offer means buying one package with supporting included-product rows
exactly one Full Field Portrait may mount the Living Core and every repeated, bundle, pricing and checkout context remains static
320 through 1440 preserve readable website contexts, usable review controls and no horizontal overflow
Olli approves, combines or requests changes to the portrait architecture and treatment allocation

humanGate.approvalQuestion: Is the portrait website-card architecture correct, which treatment becomes the everyday base, and which special treatments should survive before Phase B begins?

stopConditions: Phase B website components begin before the Phase A gate
more than one Living Core animates in a viewport
the proof returns to unexplained decorative directions
the task changes live Stripe code or pricing authority
the task enters homepage, Figma or consumer migration
notes: The first product-card-02 rebuild went prematurely into functional discovery, pricing and checkout.
Phase A round 01 was rejected because ten art-card treatments obscured the website component and included weak concepts.
Round 02 recommendation: C01 Editorial Portrait base; C02 focal, C03 dense and C04 commerce-only special treatments.
